question: Can experimental larval survival for a butterfly in the chocho 239-species cohort calibrate which listed plant-host opportunities are biologically realized, without inferring broad demographic gains from host presence?

source.article: Saldivar and Wilson Rankin 2024 Ecosphere DOI 10.1002/ecs2.4810
source.description: The mirrored deposit is the same study, not independent replication.

inclusion.status: 2=death event; 1=alive or censored, NOT adult emergence
inclusion.time: Original nonnegative numeric time, no guesswork
inclusion.rows: Each row is a distinct larval observation even when all recorded fields match.

outputs: Exact source MD5, header and record count
Per natural plant and source: n, dead, censored and measured time range
Nonparametric survival through recorded day 10 only if source definitions warrant
Explicit wild-versus-commercial larva breakdown and potential trial clustering
decision: Existing 2024 study already establishes poor survival for some plant diets and strong larval-source effects; do not claim novelty.
Do not map botanical plant presence to adult fitness or geographical butterfly colonization.
Do not pool wild and commercial larvae for a host-quality effect.
Do not equate status=1 with adult emergence.
Use only as a scale- and source-bounded realization/measurement sensitivity.
If source checksum or outcome definitions fail, stop.
